findings.claim: In a sandboxed srcdoc frame, normalizing a locked activity fragment creates a Back loop. When replaceState throws, historyChanged() falls back to assigning location.hash to the current activity, which pushes a new history entry instead of replacing the locked one. Each later Back returns to the locked entry, which is normalized by pushing again, so Back can no longer move past that point in the frame (inferred, not tested: the host page Back button traverses the same joint session history and would hit the same loop). This predates d3715dcd (the same fallback existed at 2f281e85) and is not reachable from any page control: no in-page link produces an #activity-N fragment outside the guarded timeline and back links, so it needs a host- or devtools-driven fragment change inside the frame.

evidence.section: artifact.html line 1191, historyChanged() locked-fragment normalization and its location.hash fallback (textSha256 is of that exact source line). Observation: Not driven on this page (later activities need private inputs); the handler is byte-identical to the four public pages, where it reproduced with Playwright 1.55 Chromium from the repository node_modules (no screenshots, no traces) in a sandbox="allow-scripts" srcdoc frame, where history.pushState and replaceState throw SecurityError: after reaching activity 3 through the committed public route, a locked #activity-4 fragment was normalized to #activity-2 but history.length grew by two; after Previous, seven Backs were pressed in total: the first showed activity 2, and each of the other six landed on the locked entry, was pushed forward again to #activity-2, and stayed on activity 2 with history.length fixed. Top-level (replaceState available) the same sequence walked back normally to activity 1. A probe showed location.replace with a fragment in this sandboxed srcdoc frame navigates the frame away and loses the page, so it is not a safe substitute.

findings.recommendation: When replaceState is unavailable, keep the current activity without rewriting the fragment (leave the locked fragment in place, as foreign fragments already are), or otherwise avoid adding an entry during normalization; keep the pushState-failure fallback in go() and Continue, which correctly adds an entry for real forward navigation. Note for the reconciler: leaving the locked fragment in place departs from the DESIGN.md sentence that a disallowed fragment normalizes, but in this sandbox normalization without adding an entry is not available (replaceState throws and location.replace reloads the frame), so the choice is between that sentence and a Back loop.

Loop-4 ruling on current bytes at d3715dcd (HEAD 1a645b15; sha256 1e0ee23768e584648d1f11ffd564333448633d33d9a9bf6596496291fb8c894f). historyChanged() (line 1191) now returns early for any non-empty fragment that is not #activity-N, so a foreign fragment keeps the current activity (no state change), an empty fragment still means activity 1, and a locked #activity-N fragment is rewritten to the current one. The guard is now a string holding the expected target fragment, set only around the location.hash fallback and cleared by the first popstate or hashchange whose hash equals it, so it suppresses exactly the event the page caused and cannot go stale (it is cleared again if the setter throws). Not driven past activity 1 on this page because later activities need private inputs; the navigation code is byte-identical to the four public pages, where Playwright 1.55 Chromium from the repository node_modules (no screenshots, no traces) (top-level and sandboxed srcdoc, using committed public route segments) showed foreign fragments keep the current activity without state change (the fragment stays in the URL, read as an allowed in-page anchor rather than a disallowed activity fragment), locked fragments normalize, and Continue/Back/Forward/Previous never desynchronize the fragment and the shown activity. The accepted defect is resolved. The pre-existing sandbox Back-loop in the same normalization fallback is filed separately as new low finding pyf-sme-loop4-functions-001 and does not reopen this item.

The print rule (line 157) now also shows the hidden recap section (section.pep-act without data-pep-activity), hides its workspace child, and reveals hidden [data-step] nodes inside its reading region. Not fully fixed: the same rule hides the whole recap workspace, and that workspace holds the recap's static model, a summary table inside the recap step's live-model figure. Printed from any activity, that figure does not render, and 5 of its 5 rows appear nowhere else in the printed text (body innerText under print media after beforeprint). It renders only when printing from the recap itself. So part of the recap's teaching content is still omitted from print before the learner reaches it, which is the accepted defect (DESIGN.md Print: every enrolled page prints non-empty teaching content). Recommendation: in print, show the recap workspace's model figure as well, and keep hiding only the parts that would claim completion early (the ask region with the finished line and the completion message). Open.
